# Weekly Sleep, Mood, and Exercise Visualization Plan

A simple multi-metric dashboard will show how sleep, mood, and exercise move together across the week. The clearest story here is likely a mix of daily variation and a possible positive relationship between more sleep/exercise and better mood.

## Best Chart Choices for Each Metric

- **Sleep hours**: **Line chart**
  - Best for spotting day-to-day trend, dips, and recovery.
  - Use date on the x-axis and sleep hours on the y-axis.

- **Mood score**: **Line chart**
  - Best for seeing whether mood rises after better sleep or more activity.
  - Keep the same date axis so it can be compared directly with sleep.

- **Exercise minutes**: **Bar chart**
  - Best because exercise tends to be “event-like” and varies by day.
  - Bars make high-activity days stand out clearly.

- **Sleep vs mood relationship**: **Scatter plot**
  - Best for checking whether higher sleep hours line up with higher mood scores.
  - Add a trend line if possible.

- **Exercise vs mood relationship**: **Scatter plot**
  - Best for seeing whether more active days correspond to better mood.
  - Useful for identifying whether low-activity days cluster with lower mood.

## What the Data Might Reveal

| Metric Pair | Best Chart | Likely Pattern to Check | Possible Insight |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sleep over time | Line chart | Midweek improvement after early-week dip | Sleep looks lowest on Mar 3 and strongest on Mar 6, suggesting recovery later in the week |
| Mood over time | Line chart | Mood rises and falls with sleep quality | Mood appears to track sleep fairly closely, with higher scores on better-rested days |
| Exercise over time | Bar chart | Activity peaks on a few days | Exercise is uneven, with stronger sessions on Mar 4 and Mar 6 |
| Sleep vs mood | Scatter plot | Positive relationship | Days with more sleep may align with better mood scores |
| Exercise vs mood | Scatter plot | Mild positive relationship | More active days may be associated with slightly better mood, though not perfectly |

## Pattern Interpretation

- **Early-week dip, later-week recovery**: Sleep starts lower, then improves toward the end of the week.
- **Mood appears sleep-sensitive**: The lowest mood days line up with shorter sleep, while the highest mood days come after longer sleep.
- **Exercise may support mood**: The strongest exercise days also show relatively strong mood, but the relationship is probably weaker than sleep.
- **Best overall story**: The week suggests a **positive wellness loop** where better sleep and more movement may coincide with better mood.

## Visualization Plan

1. **Top row: three small line/bar cards**
   - Sleep hours line chart
   - Mood score line chart
   - Exercise minutes bar chart

2. **Bottom row: two relationship charts**
   - Sleep vs mood scatter plot
   - Exercise vs mood scatter plot

3. **Optional annotation layer**
   - Mark the highest sleep day, highest mood day, and highest exercise day
   - Add a note for the lowest sleep/lowest mood day to highlight contrast

## Quick Actions

- Action: [Button: Build dashboard](https://www.google.com/search?q=dashboard+chart+builder+line+scatter+bar)
- Action: [Button: Correlation guide](https://www.google.com/search?q=how+to+read+correlation+scatter+plot)

## Sources

- Chart selection basics: https://www.data-to-viz.com/
- Correlation and scatter plots: https://www.khanacademy.org/math/statistics-probability/describing-relationships-quantitative-data
